Where it began

Josh Tongue was born in Redditch on 15 November 1997 and went to The King's School in Worcester. He came through at Worcestershire and played his first first-class match for the county in March 2016, against the Oxford MCC University side. A first List A game followed in May 2017.

The player

Tongue bowls right-arm and fast. England picked him for the one-off Test against Ireland in June 2023, and on the second day he took his first Test wicket and went on to five in the innings. Not many bowlers start like that.

He moved to Nottinghamshire that summer. After a year away from the game, his first match for his new county in 2025 brought 5 for 66 and his first first-class fifty in an eight-wicket win over Durham. England had him back that summer, and in three Tests against India he took 19 wickets, more than any other England bowler in the series, finishing with five in an innings at The Oval.

The 2025-26 Ashes tour went even better. He played the last three Tests and took 18 wickets, and his 7 for 89 at Melbourne made him Player of the Match. By November 2026 he had played 15 Tests and taken 76 wickets at 26.33, with four five-wicket innings and a best of 5 for 45.

What made him special

Wickets, and lots of them, whenever he has had a run in the side. His Test career has come in bursts, but each burst has been productive, and his record against India and in Australia shows a bowler who rises to the big occasion. An average of 26.33 is a fine return for a fast bowler who has done much of his work in tough series.

With the bat he is honest about his job. His 133 Test runs include a best of 30 not out, and his first-class fifty for Nottinghamshire came as something of a pleasant surprise to all concerned.

Away from the middle

His Worcestershire teammates had a soft spot for him, and a nickname to go with it: Jeevy Boy. Nottinghamshire clearly like him too. In April 2026 they agreed a new three-year deal, which runs through the 2029 season.

And finally

Some bowlers need a few Tests to find their feet. Josh Tongue took five wickets in his very first innings and, on his first Ashes tour, a Player of the Match award at Melbourne. Whatever Jeevy Boy means, it seems to suit him.
